00:00:05 - Lena: Hey team, thanks for joining, really appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick round robin intro?
00:00:12 - Sarah: Hi, Sarah Malik here, CTO at ApolloMed. We're evaluating Redwood for some clinical note summarization and triage flows. Biggest thing for us is PHI, uh, and legal/compliance boxes.
00:00:22 - Lena: Totally, yep that’s what we want to cover. Marco, can you kick off on the security posture and high level?
00:00:27 - Marco: Sure, yeah. Hey everyone. So Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 in process — um — we can send the latest attestations. We also have BAA options for HIPAA customers. On the platform side we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles by team, and audit logs that are exportable.
00:00:50 - Raj: Quick question — when you say audit logs are exportable, how long are they retained by default and can we ship them off to our SIEM?
00:00:58 - Marco: Default retention in hosted is 30 days for audit-level logs but for enterprise contracts we offer longer retention and log shipping to customer-owned S3 or syslog endpoints. We can also enable continuous export to Splunk/Datadog.
00:01:12 - Tom: Do you include request/response payloads in those logs? We need to control PHI in logs.
00:01:18 - Marco: Good point. By default, payloads are redacted in audit logs. We can configure what is captured — for enterprise with private deployments or dedicated pools, customers can choose to keep payloads off logs entirely and only store metadata.
00:01:32 - Maya: And retention for prompts and model outputs — do you ever train models on customer data? This is an absolute requirement: NO training on customer data.
00:01:41 - Lena: Short answer: we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train our base models. We have a strict policy — customer content is not used to improve open models or Redwood models unless there is an explicit opt-in and contract.
00:01:55 - Sarah: Do you have a formal data handling / training policy we can include in our vendor assessment?
00:02:00 - Lena: Yes, we'll include the training policy language in the security packet we send. It's in the security whitepaper and the BAA can state the same.
00:02:08 - Raj: For HIPAA, will Redwood sign a BAA and does private deployment change anything?
00:02:13 - Marco: We support BAAs. For HIPAA workloads customers often choose dedicated capacity or our private deployment, which isolates data plane in their VPC or on-prem. In that mode, keys and storage are completely customer-controlled — BYOK via KMS, HSM support.
00:02:27 - Raj: Does BYOK support AWS KMS and GCP KMS?
00:02:30 - Marco: Yes, we support major cloud KMS providers and a hardware-backed HSM option for dedicated/private installs.
00:02:35 - Maya: Can we see an architecture diagram of the private option, I want to confirm network boundaries and audit trails.
00:02:40 - Marco: Absolutely, I'll attach the private deployment diagram; it shows the control plane separation, vpc peering, and how request routing and KV cache stay in-customer-network.
00:02:52 - Tom: You mentioned KV cache — can you explain where the KV cache lives? Our security team is sensitive about any persistent caches with PHI.
00:03:00 - Marco: Default hosted KV cache is ephemeral in Redwood-managed nodes and is encrypted at rest. For private or dedicated, the KV cache can be provisioned in your VPC/storage and encrypted with your keys. Apologies, sometimes auto-transcripts write it as K V cash.
00:03:15 - Sarah: Thanks. On data residency: we need all PHI to remain in the US east region for now. Is that supported?
00:03:21 - Lena: Yes, we can pin deployments to regions and ensure data residency. For hosted customers we have regional controls and for enterprise we can guarantee region-specific storage in the contract.
00:03:31 - Raj: Encryption — is data encrypted in transit and at rest? How are keys managed?
00:03:36 - Marco: TLS for transit, AES-256 for rest by default, and KMS for key management. We offer BYOK so customers can supply keys; keys never leave the cloud KMS/HSM and Redwood only uses the KMS API to decrypt in a transient manner for runtime operations.
00:03:52 - Maya: Any possibility of bringing an HSM into an on-prem install?
00:03:55 - Marco: Yes, on-prem private installs can integrate with customer HSMs. We'll add HSM integration docs to the packet.
00:04:02 - Lena: On the training/no-training point, we also provide a technical control: you can disable retention of prompts/outputs entirely in your tenant settings; retention is off by default for BAA/HIPAA mode.
00:04:14 - Maya: Good. Do you have any formal attestation that customer content isn't used for training? Our procurement wants explicit contractual language.
00:04:21 - Lena: We'll include the standard clause as part of the BAA and the contract language; I'll copy the exact wording in the docs.
00:04:28 - Raj: Incident response — do you publish mean time to detect/mean time to respond or have an IR plan we can review?
00:04:33 - Marco: We have an incident response plan and run regular tabletop exercises; we can share the IR summary and escalation contacts. For enterprise customers we offer faster SLA-backed notification windows in the contract.
00:04:46 - Sarah: Pen testing and third-party attestations?
00:04:49 - Marco: We do annual pen tests and engage external firms; summary results are in the SOC2 package and we can provide a redacted penetration test summary under NDA.
00:04:59 - Tom: From infra side, we want to run a small benchmark — can you provide a benchmark harness or run a short performance test on expected payloads?
00:05:06 - Marco: Yes, we can run a mini benchmark. For sensitive workloads we can run in a dedicated pool or private deployment. We'll propose a benchmark plan that measures latency at typical sequence lengths and shows KV cache behavior and batching impact.
00:05:21 - Sarah: About logging: we need immutable audit trails for at least a year. Is that possible?
00:05:26 - Marco: Yes, for enterprise contracts we can set retention to a year or longer and ship to your S3 bucket. We support WORM-style storage if needed.
00:05:35 - Maya: Anything we should expect in the compliance questionnaire that might be a blocker?
00:05:40 - Lena: The usual: encryption, access control, data residency, incident response, details on training-on-data — none should be blockers given what we've discussed. We'll highlight the BAA and private deployment as mitigations.
00:05:51 - Raj: OK, any third-party integrations that are risky? For example, do you ever route content to external plugins or tools?
00:05:58 - Marco: No automatic external plugin routing on enterprise dedicated/private deployments. Hosted can support integrations but we can lock down routes and disable outbound integ for your tenancy.
00:06:10 - Sarah: Can we get a timeline for pilot — we want a 4-week pilot with a dedicated pool and KMS BYOK to validate latency and retention.
00:06:17 - Lena: Sounds good. We'll propose an architecture and cost for a 4-week dedicated pilot. Marco will include steps to validate no retention and the benchmark plan.
00:06:26 - Maya: Also please include the exact clause language about "no training" and retention settings so procurement can sign off.
